items.headline: Riyadh airport attack kills 12; Trump weighs joining strikes on Houthis
items.summary: Saudi authorities said a Saturday attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300, the latest of several attacks there this week. President Trump said the U.S. may join Saudi-led strikes on Yemen's Houthi rebels.

items.headline: Isaias blamed for at least two deaths in Florida and Alabama
items.summary: At least two deaths have been attributed to Hurricane Isaias after it hit Florida's coast and moved through Alabama. The storm downed trees and left hundreds of thousands of people without power.

items.headline: Firing squads gain ground as lethal injection falters
items.summary: Shortages of lethal injection drugs and several botched executions are leading officials to consider other methods of carrying out the death penalty. The debate comes as the Army prepares a firing-squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter.

items.headline: GOP donor accuses Guilfoyle of seeking $100,000 for access
items.summary: Republican donor Eric Deters alleges that Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle sought $100,000 in exchange for access to senior Trump administration officials. He says the promised access was never delivered.

items.headline: DOJ memo loosens political-activity rules for Blanche
items.summary: An internal Justice Department memo eases restrictions on political activity for Attorney General Todd Blanche and other Senate-confirmed appointees. The change comes as Blanche campaigns ahead of the midterms.

items.headline: Democrats turn to influencers to win back Latino voters
items.summary: After losing ground with Latino voters, Democrats are enlisting Latino content creators to reach voters disillusioned with both parties. The effort comes weeks before the midterm elections.

items.headline: Kennedy Center names music agent as artistic director
items.summary: The Kennedy Center's executive director appointed an agent who has worked with ZZ Top and Tommy Lee to lead the institution's programming. The choice has raised concerns about the center's direction.

items.headline: Lawsuits test claims of serious harm from GLP-1 drugs
items.summary: Ongoing lawsuits allege that GLP-1 drugs can cause serious harms such as blindness or pancreatitis. Limited data on how often these side effects occur complicates both the science and the legal cases.

items.headline: Skydance merger set to reshape Hollywood and news
items.summary: The Ellison family's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery could reshape Hollywood and the news business. The Nation argues it will mean more top-down control and less room for dissent.

items.headline: New giant waterlily species found via Instagram photo
items.summary: Researchers have documented a new species of giant waterlily. They first noticed the plant in a photo posted on Instagram.

digest.overview:
Hurricane Isaias has been blamed for at least two deaths after battering Florida and Alabama, where it downed trees and left hundreds of thousands of people without power. Republican donor Eric Deters alleged that Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle sought $100,000 in exchange for access to senior Trump officials, access he says never came. An internal Justice Department memo loosened limits on political activity for Attorney General Todd Blanche and other Senate-confirmed appointees as Blanche hits the campaign trail. Officials are weighing firing squads as lethal-injection drug shortages and botched executions mount, while experts see little legal room to challenge the planned livestream of the Fort Hood shooter's execution. The Kennedy Center named a music-industry agent as its new artistic director. Democrats are enlisting Latino content creators to win back Latino voters, and South Carolina's Senate candidates debate on Sunday. New lawsuits over GLP-1 drugs highlight how little data exists on serious side effects such as blindness.

Abroad, Saudi authorities said an attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Saturday killed 12 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in a series of strikes on the airport this week. Attacks on Saudi airports, military sites and oil facilities have intensified since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major offensive against Yemen's Houthi rebels a week ago, and President Trump said the United States may join the strikes. In Asia, South Korea and Ukraine remain at odds over two captured North Korean soldiers. In environmental news, researchers documented a new species of giant waterlily that they first spotted in a photo posted on Instagram.

home.overview:
Cleveland finished a comeback from 0–2 down, blanking the White Sox 2–0 in ALDS Game 5 behind 12 strikeouts from Gavin Williams and a two-run homer from José Ramírez; the Guardians open the ALCS at Tampa Bay on Monday. The NLCS starts tonight in Milwaukee, with Tarik Skubal facing Jacob Misiorowski. NFL Week 5 resumes with Eagles–Jaguars in London, where Philadelphia is without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, plus Bears–Packers and 49ers–Seahawks, and Tyler Huntley starts for the injured Lamar Jackson as Baltimore visits Atlanta on Sunday night. In NBA preseason, Boston routed Philadelphia 144–106.

Arsenal rallied past Leeds 2–1 and Chelsea routed Bournemouth 5–1, while Man United and Tottenham drew 1–1 ahead of Man City's trip to Liverpool today. Barcelona made it eight wins from eight with a 3–0 win over Getafe, and Real Madrid beat Villarreal 1–0 but lost Vinícius Júnior to a red card. RB Leipzig crushed Frankfurt 6–0, Bayern drew 2–2 at Augsburg and PSG beat Le Mans 3–1. In Korea, Gwangju upset Ulsan HD 4–3 and Suwon Samsung beat Ansan 4–1 behind a Lewis hat-trick.

brief: Gavin Williams struck out 12 over 5 2/3 scoreless innings and José Ramírez hit a two-run homer as Cleveland beat the White Sox 2–0 in ALDS Game 5.
The Guardians won three straight after falling behind 0–2, and their pitchers set a record with 21 strikeouts in the clincher.
Cleveland opens the ALCS at Tampa Bay on Monday at 8 p.m. ET, with Drew Rasmussen the Rays' likely Game 1 starter.
The NLCS starts tonight in Milwaukee at 8 p.m. ET, with Tarik Skubal facing Jacob Misiorowski in Game 1.
The Dodgers say they are confident Shohei Ohtani will break out of his slump against the Brewers.
